From a point P, 13 cm from the centre, a tangent is drawn to a circle of radius 5 cm. Find the tangent length (cm).
Prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through that point.
questions.modelAnswer: Let the tangent at P meet the circle only at P, with centre O. Take any other point Q on the tangent. Q is outside the circle (the tangent touches only at P), so OQ > OP. So OP is the shortest distance from O to the line, and the shortest segment from a point to a line is perpendicular to it. Hence OP ⊥ the tangent.
rubric: Other points on tangent are outside
